bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS in the server-database avatar pipeline. user.updateAvatar accepts any data:image* payload (including data:image/svg;base64,...) with no MIME allowlist or SVG sanitization, derives the object extension from the attacker-controlled subtype, and stores the bytes at user/avatar/<userId>/<uuid>.svg. GET /webapi/user/avatar/[id]/[image] then returns those bytes with Content-Type image/svg+xml (CONTENT_TYPE_MAP.svg), no Content-Disposition: attachment, no nosniff, and no script-blocking CSP. A victim who navigates to that same-origin URL (or any embed that parses the SVG as a document) executes the attacker's script in the LobeChat origin. UI avatar widgets rasterize uploads to WebP via canvas, but the tRPC mutation and CLI path do not. CVE.org CVE-2026-72594 is PUBLISHED (TuranSec, not rejected/withdrawn); GHSA-cjxw-hmxq-h489 withdrawn_at is null. Affected through v2.2.13 as stated; the same sink is still present at clone HEAD.
flaw_origin: PR #7152 added server-side avatar upload. Member bb4c4ed206bb442e2c3a991a01b7a2fcfa4fe286 first stored unrestricted data:image* bytes on S3 and exposed them via getFullFileUrl (S3 public/presigned origin). Member 7f13f6afb8e79e07a80f77dec881ba0d4c2491c6 is the BIC: it first wrote the same-origin proxy src/app/(backend)/webapi/user/avatar/[id]/[image]/route.ts mapping svg -> image/svg+xml and switched the stored avatar URL to /webapi/user/avatar/<userId>/<uuid>.<fileType>. That is the first public write of the application-origin SVG document sink. Squash f15200d348ce2c0765c1459b1a19aa2f1f63ce90 landed the same lines on main in v1.82.5. Later e7236c0169a5565c2fc01132cfed557743b48d3e only scoped old-avatar deletion URLs and still allows every data:image* prefix.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-72594/GHSA-cjxw-hmxq-h489 is a published CWE-79 for stored XSS via a crafted SVG user avatar through v2.2.13. The live mechanism is the pair of (1) updateAvatar persisting attacker-chosen data:image bytes under a derived extension and (2) the same-origin avatar GET mapping .svg to image/svg+xml without forcing download or blocking script. UI canvas-to-WebP is not a control on the tRPC/CLI API. First-party advisory references stop at the product repo; there is no vendor patch commit. BIC search used the avatar GET route and updateAvatar, then git log --follow/-L and PR #7152 members rather than scanning for AI authors. The squash on main is f15200d348ce2c0765c1459b1a19aa2f1f63ce90; protocol forbids treating that aggregate as BIC. Reconstructable member 7f13f6afb8e79e07a80f77dec881ba0d4c2491c6 is the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable serving lines; its parent 5f0e6469bcb56de93164fc7c9b7ce42c702aaa0c lacks the route and still served avatars off S3. AI is judged only on that BIC commit object: human RICHQAQ, no AI authorship/co-authorship trailers. Therefore NOT_AI. No public fix exists through clone HEAD, so fix_sha/direct_fix_sha remain null with an explicit unpatched record.

Potential fix: MIME-allowlist raster images only, drop svg from CONTENT_TYPE_MAP, and serve avatars with attachment + nosniff + CSP script-src 'none'.

unpatched.reason: CVE-2026-72594 lists affected through v2.2.13 with no patched version; GHSA-cjxw-hmxq-h489 has unknown patched versions; avatar GET still maps svg to image/svg+xml and updateAvatar still accepts any data:image* at clone HEAD 452a0896b28b92f24dc3ef4ed984dd486f34a6bb (2026-08-24) and v2.2.14.

potential_fix.approach: In updateAvatar, allowlist only non-scriptable raster MIME types (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif) and reject image/svg and image/svg+xml; rasterize any accepted image server-side. Remove svg from CONTENT_TYPE_MAP in the avatar GET route (or always emit image/png). Add Content-Disposition: attachment, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none'; sandbox on that route.
potential_fix.rationale: The XSS fires because attacker-controlled SVG is stored and then served as an executable image/svg+xml document on the application origin. Blocking SVG at upload and never labeling leftover objects as SVG XML closes the sink even if a victim opens the avatar URL.
